# Chatbot Flow Design — intent architecture, grounding, fallbacks and human escalation

Curated by Skill Harbor — @rampstackco's chatbot-flow-design: a senior growth practitioner's playbook for designing conversational flows for website chatbots and AI agents — intent recognition architecture, branching logic, fallback handling, escalation to human, conversation analytics. The keystone framing: scripted-bots (rigid trees that fail edge cases) vs hallucinating-bots (LLM without structure that makes things up) vs structured-guided-conversation (LLM-powered with intent architecture, knowledge-base grounding and fallback discipline — the goal). Covers the chatbot decision (when a bot earns deployment and when it doesn't), intent design patterns and coverage targets (70–90%), RAG-style grounding and citation discipline, multi-layered fallbacks (clarify → suggest → resource handoff → human escalation), escalation triggers with clean context handoff, per-intent analytics, common failure modes, and a 12-point design framework. Honest caveats: explicitly design-only — it distinguishes chatbot DESIGN (this skill) from chatbot IMPLEMENTATION (engineering work handed off via specs); it references sibling skills in its series (ai-content-collaboration, integration-orchestrator, pm-spec-writing) and bundled references/ files that ship with the repo. The skill's frontmatter states no license; the catalog manifest records MIT — manifest takes precedence. MIT licensed per the manifest. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
